latest_week.new_features_summary: New runtime_events counters and corrupt-stream handling, safer Weak.get_copy, Set sharing optimizations, and a Win32 UNC realpath fix.
latest_week.new_features:
- **Weak.get_copy** no longer copies continuations, since copying a continuation is unsafe ([#14988](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14988)) by [Jeremy Yallop](https://github.com/yallop); [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) followed up by opening a PR to deprecate `Weak.get_copy` outright ([#15064](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15064)).
- The **expansiveness check** now takes effect cases into account, closing a soundness gap around `match ... with effect ...` ([#14986](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14986)) by [Jeremy Yallop](https://github.com/yallop).
- The **Lambda IR** no longer trusts GADT equations introduced by refutable/partial-match arguments, fixing a native-code segfault from invalid value kinds ([#15035](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15035), closing [#14898](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14898)) by [Florian Angeletti](https://github.com/Octachron).
- **Runtime_events** gains new counters `EV_C_MAJOR_DIRECT_ALLOCATED_WORDS`, `EV_C_MAJOR_SUSPENDED_ALLOCATED_WORDS` and `EV_C_MAJOR_RESUMED_ALLOCATED_WORDS`, plus an `EV_EXPLICIT_GC_RAMP_UP` span covering `Gc.ramp_up` calls ([#15001](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15001)) by [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist).
- **Runtime_events** consumers no longer see spurious "corrupt stream" failures when they fall behind the producer; an overwritten ring slot is now reported as lost events instead ([#15016](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15016), closing [#14151](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14151)) by [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist).
- **Set.union**, **Set.inter** and **Set.diff** got better complexity on physically-shared sets, avoiding unnecessary traversal/allocation and preserving sharing when the result is unchanged ([#15009](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15009)) by [Nicolás Ojeda Bär](https://github.com/nojb).
- **Unix.realpath** now normalizes Win32 UNC paths correctly, e.g. `\\?\UNC\server\share` maps to `\\server\share` instead of `UNC\server\share` ([#15056](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15056), closing [#15044](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15044)) by [Nicolás Ojeda Bär](https://github.com/nojb).
- Parser precedence for the **`with module type`** constraint was fixed so that `T with module type S = X -> X` parses as `T with module type S = (X -> X)` ([#14978](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14978)) by [314eter](https://github.com/314eter).
- The **power backend** now emits `fsqrt` directly for square root instead of calling into C, matching the earlier riscv change ([#15006](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15006)) by [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham).
- **libunix** build fixes for Cygwin/mingw covering missing `gethostname`/IPv6 guards, blocking sections around `realpath`/`lockf`, and missing root registration ([#14740](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14740), [#14921](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14921)) by [Antonin Décimo](https://github.com/MisterDA).
- **CONTRIBUTING.md** was updated to add [Stefan Muenzel](https://github.com/smuenzel) as a maintainer ([#15057](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15057)) and to mention the possibility of writing an RFC before a large change, alongside a flattened list of alternative ways to contribute ([#15055](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15055)) by [Raphaël Proust](https://github.com/raphael-proust).
- **HACKING.adoc** dropped the `opam-custom-install`-based workflow instructions, keeping only the simpler `opam install . --assume-built` path ([#15041](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15041)) by [Raphaël Proust](https://github.com/raphael-proust).
latest_week.activity_summary: Eleven new PRs opened spanning codegen, tooling and governance, alongside ongoing link-time-linking, GC-pacing and Hashtbl redesign proposals.
latest_week.activity:
- Eleven **PRs were opened this week and remain open**, covering codegen (dead-code elimination of discarded atomic loads by [Xavier Clerc](https://github.com/xclerc), [#15045](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15045)), tooling (`ocamllex` cleanup of generated output on a fatal missing-case warning by [cui fliter](https://github.com/cuishuang), [#15048](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15048); a new `EV_PROCESS_CREATE` lifecycle event and CI curl-retry/opam-validation hardening by [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist), [#15049](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15049), [#15050](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15050)), typing (an escaped-`Equality_trace` fix by [Samuel Vivien](https://github.com/samsa1), [#15052](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15052); a `[@@deprecated_unlabelled]` attribute proposal for gracefully deprecating unlabelled arguments by [Nicolás Ojeda Bär](https://github.com/nojb), [#15054](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15054)), scheduling (always advancing the work counter in idle slices by [Nick Barnes](https://github.com/NickBarnes), [#15062](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15062)), governance (retiring inactive maintainers by [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche), [#15063](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15063); deprecating `Weak.get_copy`, [#15064](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15064)), CI (disabling the beyond-2038 support check on 32-bit CI by [Olivier Nicole](https://github.com/OlivierNicole), [#15065](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15065)), and testing (skipping the AFL fuzz test when not built with `--with-afl` by [@akashchamp](https://github.com/akashchamp), [#15066](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15066), addressing [#15046](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15046)).
- [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27) opened parsetree support for wildcards/holes in simple expressions and module expressions ([#15051](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15051)), which merged just after this reporting window closed.
- **Runtime_events** continues to see concentrated work from [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist): beyond the merged allocation counters and corrupt-stream fix above, open work includes documentation improvements ([#15039](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15039)) and handling of lost-word truncation reporting ([#15010](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15010)).
- Three **OSEC security-advisory reference** PRs were merged in quick succession by [Hannes Mehnert](https://github.com/hannesm) ([#15059](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15059), [#15060](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15060), [#15061](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15061)).
- Backend/codegen work continued with an open PR to drop redundant memory-model fences around atomic RMWs on AArch64 by [Sebastian Pop](https://github.com/sebpop) ([#14936](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14936)), and a proposal to emit `clz`/`ctz` bit-counting as C primitives on amd64 and arm64 by [Zane Hambly](https://github.com/Zaneham) ([#15018](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15018)).
- Larger in-flight proposals remain open, including [Raphaël Proust](https://github.com/raphael-proust)'s link-time linking design that lets users rewrite the linker invocation via `-linking-variant` ([#14895](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14895)), [Damien Doligez](https://github.com/damiendoligez)'s new GC-pacing logic ([#14796](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14796)), [Vincent Laviron](https://github.com/lthls)'s support for an unlimited number of non-constant constructors ([#14507](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14507)), [Florian Angeletti](https://github.com/Octachron)'s structured diagnostics for the compiler ([#13766](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/13766)), and [Jeannalyse](https://github.com/Jeannalyse)'s new `Hashtbl` implementation ([#14956](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14956)) and `Atomic.compare_and_exchange` addition ([#14912](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14912)).
- Two long-dormant PRs were closed this week: an RFC to add a single file to the load path ([#9056](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/9056)) by [Nicolás Ojeda Bär](https://github.com/nojb), and `Lambda.shallow_fold_left` ([#8784](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/8784)) by [Vladimir Keleshev](https://github.com/keleshev).
latest_week.discussions_summary: Discussions covered merging flexdll into the compiler repo, AI-tool transparency after a Claude-filed issue, and new/retiring maintainers.
latest_week.notable_discussions:
- [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27) proposed at the maintainer meeting merging **flexdll** into the compiler repository rather than keeping it as a submodule, to simplify maintenance while preserving flexlink's standalone-linker use case ([#15058](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15058)); [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) noted the general usability pain of git submodules.
- Issue [#15043](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15043) (a `runtime_events` ring-buffer hang) prompted a discussion about AI-tool transparency after [Sadiq Jaffer](https://github.com/sadiqj) explained the detailed report had been filed autonomously by a Claude instance he had pointed at the ring-buffer code; [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) asked for transparency about tool-produced issue text going forward, and the underlying bug was confirmed as real, with [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist) landing the fix ([#15016](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15016)).
- Governance changes were discussed and merged this week: [Stefan Muenzel](https://github.com/smuenzel) was added as a maintainer in recognition of steady contributions to the backend and type-checker ([#15057](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15057)), while [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) opened a companion PR to retire five long-inactive maintainers ([#15063](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15063)).
- The **Windows stop-the-world barrier** report from [Daniel Larraz](https://github.com/daniel-larraz) ([#15042](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15042)) drew a detailed root-cause discussion from [Antonin Décimo](https://github.com/MisterDA), pointing to `Sleep`'s millisecond resolution in `caml_plat_spin_back_off` and proposing a high-resolution waitable timer; [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) suggested a quick test by skipping `Sleep` below the clock granularity.
- [Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac](https://github.com/panglesd) and [Florian Angeletti](https://github.com/Octachron) worked through a subtle discrepancy between interface- and implementation-context typing of a functor argument alias ([#15047](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15047)), tracing it to the uninhabited module type produced when module aliases are used on functor arguments.
latest_week.trends_summary: Runtime_events tooling, Windows robustness, GADT soundness edge cases, and non-x86 backend parity remain recurring themes.
latest_week.emerging_trends:
- **Runtime_events** continues to be an active area, with counters, corrupt-stream handling, lifecycle events and documentation all touched this week by [Tim McGilchrist](https://github.com/tmcgilchrist) ([#15001](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15001), [#15016](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15016), [#15039](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15039), [#15049](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15049), [#15010](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15010)) and surfacing a ring-buffer hang report ([#15043](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15043)).
- **Windows/Win32 robustness** remains a recurring theme, spanning the stop-the-world barrier latency report ([#15042](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15042)), the `Unix.realpath` UNC-path fix ([#15056](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15056)), Cygwin/mingw libunix build fixes ([#14740](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14740), [#14921](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14921)), and an open fix for a win32 `select` handle leak ([#14975](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14975)).
- **GADT/type-soundness edge cases** keep surfacing, from the Lambda-IR value-kind segfault fix ([#15035](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15035), closing [#14898](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14898)) to open reports on module-type subtyping with present/absent aliases ([#13976](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/13976)) and incompleteness in shadowed-module typechecking ([#14106](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14106)).
- **Non-x86 backend parity** work continued with power now emitting `fsqrt` directly ([#15006](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15006), following the earlier riscv change), AArch64 atomic-fence pruning ([#14936](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14936)), and a proposal for `clz`/`ctz` primitives on amd64/arm64 ([#15018](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15018)).
- **Project governance** saw concrete action this week, with a new maintainer added and inactive ones proposed for retirement in the same cycle ([#15057](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15057), [#15063](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15063)), plus contributor-facing documentation tightened ([#15041](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15041), [#15055](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15055)).
latest_week.issues_summary: Two approachable, well-scoped issues: ocamlmklib's -L ordering and a testsuite fix for AFL without --with-afl.
latest_week.good_first_issues:
- **`ocamlmklib` reverses the order of `-L` library-path options**, breaking intended search precedence; [Nicolás Ojeda Bär](https://github.com/nojb) confirmed it should just be fixed, and there's background research and an existing draft to build on ([#14172](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/14172), draft PR [#14173](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/14173)) by [Alexandre DOUARD](https://github.com/VecoMr).
- **`testsuite/tests/afl-instrumentation` fails whenever AFL is installed but OCaml wasn't configured with `--with-afl`**; [Xavier Leroy](https://github.com/xavierleroy) suggested simply disabling the test in that configuration, and a first attempt is already up for review ([#15046](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/issues/15046), PR [#15066](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml/pull/15066)) by [@akashchamp](https://github.com/akashchamp).

latest_week.new_features:
- Fixed a **2.6 performance regression** where `.tar.gz` repositories were opened and read twice per package during installation, saving roughly 500ms per package install; includes a refactor of `get_extra_files` in `opamFile.ml` to skip the lookup entirely when `extra-files` is empty and a new debug log on archive reads in `opamTar.ml` ([#7131](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7131) by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate))
- **Release script fixes** ensuring 32-bit binaries use the correct architecture: x86_32 binaries now take full advantage of i686 and arm32 binaries are built as armhf instead of armv7 ([#7120](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7120) by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate))
- Upgraded the autoconf-generated `configure` script to **autoconf 2.72**, moving the Hygiene CI workflow to Ubuntu 26.04 to match the available package version ([#7052](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7052) by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate))
- Added **opam 2.6.0~rc1** to the install scripts (`shell/install.sh`, `shell/install.ps1`) ([#7135](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7135) by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate))
- Added an exhaustive reftest covering the behaviour of the `conflicts` field, guarding against future regressions ([#7127](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7127) by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate))
- Version bumped to `2.7.0~alpha1~dev`, opening the next development cycle after the 2.6.0~rc1 release ([#7064](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7064) by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate))
- Published the **opam 2.6.0~rc1** release itself, after an ordering mistake caught during the release process was corrected between [#7129](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7129) and [#7134](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7134) (both by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate))
latest_week.activity_summary: Nine PRs opened including Haiku portability and switch-show fixes, alongside the 2.6.0~rc1 release cycle and ongoing repository-loading rework.
latest_week.activity:
- **Nine new PRs opened** this week: explicit Haiku OS support by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) ([#7138](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7138)), a fix making `opam switch show` fail on a non-installed switch by [Abhay Chaudhary](https://github.com/Abhayindia) ([#7139](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7139), closing [#7075](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7075)), and a migration of `OpamStd.Map.update` to the stdlib implementation by [Nathan Rebours](https://github.com/NathanReb) ([#7130](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7130), closing [#4915](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/4915)) which went through detailed style review from [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) and merged just after the week closed
- Several **draft release-engineering PRs** opened by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) remain in progress: arm64 binaries for FreeBSD/OpenBSD/NetBSD ([#7137](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7137)), upgrading the release lockfile to use OCaml 5 by default on 64-bit platforms ([#7136](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7136)), a speed-up of `OpamFile.OPAM.*equal` for strictly-equal parameters ([#7124](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7124)), and consolidating the release script to reuse `make compiler` ([#7121](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7121))
- The **2.6.0~rc1 release cycle** completed this week: [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) merged the tar.gz double-read performance fix ([#7131](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7131)), the autoconf 2.72 upgrade ([#7052](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7052)), the 2.7.0 dev-version bump ([#7064](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7064)), and the release itself after re-doing it once an ordering issue was caught ([#7129](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7129), [#7134](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7134)), with [R. Boujbel](https://github.com/rjbou) reviewing the conflicts-field reftest ([#7127](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7127))
- **Incremental repository loading** continues to be reworked across two alternative long-running draft PRs addressing the same bug where subdirectories outside `packages/` get scanned unnecessarily: [R. Boujbel](https://github.com/rjbou)'s simplification ([#6871](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/6871)) and [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate)'s homogenization of initial and diff-based loads ([#6924](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/6924)), both targeting [#6872](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6872)
- Documentation PRs explaining how opam chooses a default compiler and how to pass configure-time options to `opam switch create` remain open pending updates, addressing [#6407](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6407) and [#6645](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6645) respectively ([#6778](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/6778), [#6777](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/6777))
- New bug reports opened this week: unlisted `files/` directory entries not copied to the build directory when installing from a 1.2-format repository, related to the [#7131](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7131) fix ([#7132](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7132) by [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate)), and a request to add a `<pkg:` reftest helper that avoids triggering an unwanted `opam update` ([#7133](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7133) by [R. Boujbel](https://github.com/rjbou), with [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) suggesting removing the `<pkg:` syntax entirely instead)
latest_week.discussions_summary: Discussions covered per-package metadata storage for tools like odoc, and integrating opam-audit security-vulnerability warnings into opam.
latest_week.notable_discussions:
- [Gabriel Scherer](https://github.com/gasche) opened a discussion relaying [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam)'s OCaml Workshop 2026 talk proposal that opam expose (1) a way to query which dependency versions were actually installed for a package and (2) a generic per-package key-value metadata store, so tools like odoc could cache generated `.odoc` files on demand instead of every package installing them; discussed with [Florian Angeletti](https://github.com/Octachron) ([#7112](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/discussions/7112))
- [Hannes Mehnert](https://github.com/hannesm) proposed integrating [opam-audit](https://github.com/hannesm/opam-audit) into opam so `opam update`/`opam install` would warn about known-vulnerable packages; [Kate](https://github.com/kit-ty-kate) pushed back on adding a second security-advisory repository format and raised concerns about warning fatigue, suggesting instead a `security-advisories` URL field per repository with severity-based filtering via `opam option` ([#7113](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7113))
latest_week.trends_summary: Release engineering and portability work dominated, alongside continued install-path performance tuning and repository-loading correctness fixes.
latest_week.emerging_trends:
- **Release engineering and portability** remain a focus, spanning explicit Haiku support ([#7138](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7138)), 32-bit architecture correctness ([#7120](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7120)), arm64 BSD binaries ([#7137](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7137)), and the autoconf 2.72 upgrade ([#7052](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7052))
- **Install-path performance** continues to be scrutinized, following the tar.gz double-read fix ([#7131](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7131)) with a further speed-up proposed for `OpamFile.OPAM.*equal` ([#7124](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/7124))
- **Repository loading correctness** around incremental diff-based loads is being addressed via two competing long-running drafts rather than a single quick fix ([#6871](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/6871), [#6924](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/pull/6924), tracked in [#6872](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/6872))
- Growing interest in **supply-chain security tooling**, with proposals to integrate vulnerability auditing ([#7113](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7113)) and to investigate landlock(7) as a lighter-weight sandboxing alternative to bubblewrap ([#7140](https://github.com/ocaml/opam/issues/7140))

latest_week.brief_summary: Rudi Grinberg merged 18 PRs adding constructor/whole-call completion snippets, interactive destruct bodies, and .mli go-to-implementation.
latest_week.new_features_summary: New completion snippets for constructors and whole calls, interactive destruct bodies, and .mli go-to-implementation support.
latest_week.new_features:
- Constructor application completions offering parenthesized snippets with independent argument placeholders for OCaml constructors with payloads, alongside existing name-only completions, by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#2212](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2212))
- Destruct-generated branch bodies made independently editable snippet placeholders for clients with snippet edit support, by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#2204](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2204))
- Whole-call completions for OCaml functions with two or more labelled or optional arguments, inserting a snippet with independent placeholders for each argument, by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#2199](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2199))
- `textDocument/implementation` support for type declarations in `.mli` interface files, resolving nested modules, functor results, includes, and aliases, by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg), closing [#1163](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1163) ([#2074](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2074))
- **Semantic highlighting** now classifies function parameters and labelled/optional argument modifiers ([#1857](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/1857)) and distinguishes predeclared built-in types from user-defined ones ([#1858](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/1858), fixes [#1139](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1139)), both by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg)
- Fixed overlapping semantic tokens emitted for `with type` constraints and destructive substitutions on qualified names, by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#2206](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2206))
- Fixed the inline code action to skip constructing edits for bindings with no applicable inline uses, avoiding stack exhaustion when printing deeply recovered expressions, by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) ([#2041](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2041))
latest_week.activity_summary: Three new PRs remain open including a follow-up inline-reduction fix and an interactive rename feature, alongside an extensive test-first workflow.
latest_week.activity:
- Three PRs opened this week remain unmerged: an automated `flake.lock` dependency update ([#2216](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2216)), a follow-up fix reducing partial applications of unlabelled functions in the inline code action ([#2214](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2214)), and a feature letting users interactively rename the generated variable or function name after **Extract local** or **Extract function** via a shared snippet placeholder ([#2207](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2207)), all by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg)
- URI normalization work by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) remains open, canonicalizing equivalent URI spellings for comparison, hashing, and serialization while preserving case-sensitive POSIX double-leading paths ([#2023](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2023))
- [opale](https://github.com/N1ark)'s PR making odoc cross-references in documentation comments navigable via `textDocument/documentLink` remains open with a merge conflict, fixing [#436](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/436); the author notes the implementation was largely LLM-drafted under their direction and review ([#2139](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2139))
- Extensive test-first workflow around the **Inline into uses** code action: reproduction tests for redundant parameters in partial applications ([#2208](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2208)) were followed by coverage of scope and evaluation order ([#2209](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2209)), mutable instance variables ([#2213](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2213)), annotated mutable arguments and object `self` ([#2215](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2215)), and finally the reduction fix itself ([#2214](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2214)), all by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg)
- A similar test-then-fix pattern applied to semantic highlighting overlap, with a reproduction PR ([#2205](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2205)) merged just before the fix ([#2206](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2206))
- Additional merged test-only coverage included interface-lookup contracts ahead of go-to-implementation ([#2201](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2201)), URI escaping and operator documentation rendering ([#2210](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2210)), cleared Dune diagnostics after Merlin 5.8.1's load-path fix ([#2211](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2211)), and missing record-field deprecation flags on completions ([#2203](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2203)), all by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg)
- An automated `flake.lock` update bumping the pinned `merlin`, `nixpkgs`, and `ocaml-overlays` inputs was merged ([#2144](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2144))
- Issue [#1163](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/issues/1163) requesting **go to implementation** support on `.mli` files, opened by [Tianyi Song](https://github.com/tysg) in 2023, was closed this week once [#2074](https://github.com/ocaml/ocaml-lsp/pull/2074) merged

latest_week.brief_summary: Dune shipped breaking read-only file/cache and RPC API changes while driving the action-plugin dynamic-run RPC migration forward.
latest_week.new_features_summary: Read-only generated files/cache metadata, dynamic-run multi-invocation and dependency batching, and module pform crash fixes.
latest_week.new_features:
- BREAKING CHANGE: **generated files** are now always made read-only, even under `dune-project` language versions before 2.4, keeping shared-cache hardlink and copy modes consistent ([#16388](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16388), [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg))
- **Shared-cache metadata files** are now written read-only to guard against accidental modification, with the read-only attribute restored after Windows hardlink cleanup ([#16393](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16393), [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg))
- Breaking API change: `Dune_rpc_lwt.V1.Action_plugin.run` now returns `unit Lwt.t` instead of driving the event loop or exiting the process, letting plugin execution compose with other Lwt computations ([#16404](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16404), [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg))
- **Dynamic actions** (`dynamic-run`) can now issue multiple invocations composed sequentially with `progn` or in parallel with `concurrent` ([#16403](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16403)), honor the enclosing `with-accepted-exit-codes` policy instead of always requiring a zero exit ([#16402](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16402)), and expose `Action_plugin.build_deps` for explicit file, directory, and glob dependency batches ([#16394](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16394)) — all by [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg)
- Fixed crashes expanding module artifact pforms such as `%{cmi:...}`, `%{cmt:...}`, and `%{cmti:...}` with `(include_subdirs qualified)`; modules can now be referenced by dotted logical paths like `%{cmi:Sub_a.Foo}` ([#14498](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/14498), [#16214](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16214), [Ali Caglayan](https://github.com/Alizter), [Antonio Nuno Monteiro](https://github.com/anmonteiro))
- Melange builds now fall back to Melange module artifacts for `%{cmi:...}`, `%{cmt:...}`, and `%{cmti:...}` when no OCaml module is selected, preferring OCaml when a module exists in both modes ([#16339](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16339), [Antonio Nuno Monteiro](https://github.com/anmonteiro))
- Fixed `dynamic-run` actions ignoring `with-stdout-to` redirection, so plugin stdout now reaches the requested target instead of Dune's terminal ([#16376](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16376), [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg))
- Added validation rejecting invalid identifiers instead of crashing: Menhir `merge_into` target names ([#16387](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16387)), custom `toplevel` names ([#16373](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16373)), and `.`/`..` as `melange.emit` targets ([#16371](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16371)) — all by [Antonio Nuno Monteiro](https://github.com/anmonteiro)
- Performance improvement in Stdune's `Appendable_list` traversals (`length`, `iter`) by reusing existing child lists instead of allocating concat wrappers, cutting a 100,000-element microbenchmark from 500,000 allocated words to zero ([#16381](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16381), [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg))
- Added `Temp.with_temp_file_fd` in Stdune for scoped temporary-file descriptors with automatic close/unlink cleanup ([#16397](https://github.com/ocaml/dune/issues/16397), [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg))

latest_week.brief_summary: odoc merged 13 PRs focused on `.odoc`/`.odocl` size and CPU reduction, `include functor` rendering, and several xref/rendering bug fixes.
latest_week.new_features_summary: New `include functor` rendering plus payload compression, doc-comment memoization, and word-run merging shrink `.odoc`/`.odocl` files and cut CPU/RSS.
latest_week.new_features:
- Items included via `include functor` are now displayed as included via the functor, improving generated documentation for OxCaml code by [Marek Kubica](https://github.com/Leonidas-from-XIV) ([#1452](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1452))
- `.odoc` and `.odocl` files are now **compressed** when the compiler supports it, giving a roughly 4-5x reduction in file size, by [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) ([#1486](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1486))
- **Doc-comment parsing is memoized** and rebuilding is skipped during linking when nothing needs resolving, reducing odoc_driver user CPU by ~13%, total CPU by ~5%, and peak RSS by up to 16% on heavily templated OxCaml code, by [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) ([#1480](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1480))
- Comment text is now stored as one node per run of words instead of one per word, further shrinking `.odoc`/`.odocl` files, by [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) ([#1488](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1488))
- Removed an internal id-wrapping optimisation that was no longer needed, cutting overall disk usage by around 30% with no speed regression, by [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) ([#1479](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1479))
- The **shape reducer** is now built once and its caches shared instead of being rebuilt repeatedly, substantially reducing allocation during source resolution, by [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) ([#1487](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1487))
- Fixed loss of items bound by an `open struct ... end` following a top-of-file docstring, and fixed resolution of paths through such extended-open bindings, by [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) ([#1482](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1482))
- Fixed the canonical-path search so an unresolved `@canonical` tag no longer aborts the search for a valid canonical path, enabling wrapper modules that don't re-export every library module, by [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) ([#1483](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1483))
- Fixed a hidden-name check bug where a resolved type path could stay visible even though the type's own name was hidden, not just its parent's, by [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) ([#1484](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1484))
- Fixed optional arguments rendering as `?arg:???` for modules without an `.mli` when compiled with OCaml 5.5, which wraps optional arguments in a `TPoly` constructor, by [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) ([#1489](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1489))
- Fixed magic-string version checking so a version string that is a prefix of the on-disk one no longer causes a bad-length unmarshal failure, by [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) ([#1375](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1375))
- Updated Sherlodoc's cram tests for tyxml 5.0.0 and added a `tyxml >= 5.0` test-only constraint so contributors on tyxml 4.6 aren't surprised by CI failures, by [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) ([#1490](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1490))
- Removed the unused `` `Forward `` constructor from the internal path representation after confirming via testing it was dead code, by [Marek Kubica](https://github.com/Leonidas-from-XIV) ([#1478](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1478))

latest_week.discussions_summary: Reviewers debated the maintainability of the new memoization cache and dbuenzli asked odoc to stop running Sherlodoc tests against the public opam-repository CI.
latest_week.notable_discussions:
- [Daniel Bünzli](https://github.com/dbuenzli) asked the team not to run Sherlodoc's tyxml-version-sensitive tests in public CIs such as opam-repository, since failures there are disruptive to unrelated contributors and can break on new tyxml releases; [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) agreed to fix CI now and revisit the testing strategy before the next release ([#1490](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1490))
- [Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac](https://github.com/panglesd) raised maintainability concerns about the new doc-comment memoization cache, noting it could be confusing if adding a single reference to a large text suddenly changes generation time, and that future warnings on "malformed code blocks" would need to remember to update the memoization key list ([#1480](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1480))
- [Jules Aguillon](https://github.com/Julow) confirmed for [Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac](https://github.com/panglesd) that changes to odoc-parser's internal AST generally don't affect OCamlformat, which vendors odoc-parser, unless OCamlformat becomes sensitive to specific syntax changes ([#1488](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1488))
- Review on the id-wrapper removal touched on a hardcoded value derived from OCaml's runtime value representation, which [Paul-Elliot Anglès d'Auriac](https://github.com/panglesd) called "frightening" though ultimately approved as understandable ([#1479](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1479))
latest_week.trends_summary: This week's work was dominated by reducing `.odoc`/`.odocl` disk footprint and odoc_driver CPU/memory usage, largely motivated by OxCaml's heavily templated code.

- [Jon Ludlam](https://github.com/jonludlam) opened issues aimed at making `odoc_driver` easier to use without a full package install, suggesting upcoming driver-usability work ([#1491](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1491), [#1492](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1492), [#1461](https://github.com/ocaml/odoc/issues/1461))

latest_week.brief_summary: Introcaml runtime-introspection build support merged alongside a Safari 17 static-field bug fix and several Wasm/bigarray correctness fixes.
latest_week.new_features_summary: Introcaml build support, wasm_of_ocaml `--setenv`, and fixes for Safari static fields, bigarray access, and reference unboxing.
latest_week.new_features:
- Compiler and runtime support for building against **Introcaml**, an OCaml fork that instruments values for runtime introspection: parses the new `NEXT_RESERVED_BITS` instruction and extended `Const_block`, skips the extra reserved header bits when unmarshaling, and provides stubs for the new runtime primitives, all gated behind a new `introspect` build-time flag exposed through `Config` and the `//If:`/`(@if $introspect ...)` preprocessor directives, by [Frédéric Bour](https://github.com/let-def) and [@hhugo](https://github.com/hhugo) ([#2409](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2409))
- **wasm_of_ocaml** gained a `--setenv` flag to set environment variables read via `Sys.getenv` both by the static evaluator and at runtime, by [Jérôme Vouillon](https://github.com/vouillon) ([#2415](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2415))
- The Wasm runtime now uses a **single linear memory** instead of four separate ones (the `jsstring.wat` scratch buffer, the zstd and blake2 implementations, and wasi libc), since Safari does not support modules with multiple memories, by [Jérôme Vouillon](https://github.com/vouillon) ([#2405](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2405))
- Fixed a Safari 17 JavaScriptCore parsing bug where a line break after `static` in a generated class body caused the field to be read as an instance field named `static` rather than a class-element modifier, breaking `Int64.of_string` on values touching `MlInt64.UNSIGNED_MAX`; `static` now prints with a non-breaking space so it always stays on the same line as the element it modifies, reported and fixed by first-time contributor [habakan](https://github.com/habakan) ([#2421](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2421), fixes [#2420](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2420))
- Fixed specialized generic bigarray accesses in Wasm output (`Bigarray.Genarray.get`/`set` with a locally allocated index array), where the tag offset of the index array was applied twice, causing reads one field too far or out-of-bounds access, by [Jérôme Vouillon](https://github.com/vouillon) ([#2427](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2427))
- Fixed reference unboxing to follow substitution chains, correcting cases where a variable read from an unboxed reference was stored into another unboxed reference inside a nested closure, by [Jérôme Vouillon](https://github.com/vouillon) ([#2426](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2426))
- Fixed toplevel relocation of unit names when `use-js-string` is disabled, converting unit names to OCaml strings before the relocation callback, by [Jérôme Vouillon](https://github.com/vouillon) ([#2429](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2429))
- Preserved leading BOMs when converting OCaml strings to JavaScript strings by enabling `ignoreBOM: true` on `TextDecoder`, by [Jérôme Vouillon](https://github.com/vouillon) ([#2414](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2414))
- Fixed typed array constructors to take a `number_t js_array t` instead of a `float js_array t`, by [Jérôme Vouillon](https://github.com/vouillon) ([#2416](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2416))
- Fixed the `;;@` sourcemap annotation emitted before each Wasm function, which `Format.sprintf` was silently dropping (debug output only), by [Jérôme Vouillon](https://github.com/vouillon) ([#2424](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2424))
- Fixed sourcemap support detection on Windows, where a Unix-only `/dev/null` redirect made the Binaryen capability probe always fail and silently disabled sourcemaps; now uses `Filename.null`, by [Jérôme Vouillon](https://github.com/vouillon) ([#2418](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2418))
- Fixed the toplevel build against tyxml 5, which adds an `s` (strikethrough) element that shadowed a local string argument named `s` in the colorize helpers, by [@hhugo](https://github.com/hhugo) ([#2425](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2425))
latest_week.activity_summary: New work opened on Introcaml-based introspection, base64-encoded binary constants, ASI parsing, and Wasm toplevel splitting; ongoing Web Audio/Media Capture bindings and OxCaml/Wax efforts continued.
latest_week.activity:
- Five **PRs opened this week remain unmerged**: a prototype extending Introcaml support to full JavaScript runtime introspection with a printable-value scheme and DevTools formatter discussion by [@hhugo](https://github.com/hhugo) ([#2430](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2430)), a temporary companion PR building the benchmark image against the Introcaml switch to measure its overhead ([#2431](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2431)), a compiler change to emit large binary string constants (ocamllex/ocamlyacc/menhir tables, embedded cmis, marshaled data) as base64 literals instead of escaped strings, cutting a 30MB toplevel bundle to 26MB ([#2432](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2432)), a fix for ASI over-insertion after `async`/`using` used as plain identifiers rather than keywords ([#2422](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2422)), and a new `Split_toplevel` Wasm pass that outlines runs of instructions with no live locals into separate functions so optimizing compilers like Binaryen and TurboFan do not choke on huge toplevel functions ([#2423](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2423))
- The **Introcaml build-support PR** ([#2409](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2409)) originally opened by [Frédéric Bour](https://github.com/let-def) was rebased and extended by [@hhugo](https://github.com/hhugo) with build-time `Config` flags and a fix for `input_value: ill-formed message` errors during unmarshaling on the Introcaml switch, then merged
- **Wasm/Safari compatibility** work continued with the single-linear-memory change ([#2405](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2405)), generic bigarray access fix ([#2427](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2427)), and sourcemap fixes ([#2417](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2417), [#2418](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2418), [#2424](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2424)), all by [Jérôme Vouillon](https://github.com/vouillon)
- Ongoing work updated this week but not yet merged includes **OxCaml updates** ([#2342](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2342)), a switch to **Wax for runtime files** ([#2373](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2373)), running test suites under **bun** in CI ([#2413](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2413)), all by [Jérôme Vouillon](https://github.com/vouillon), and **Web Audio, Media Capture, and MediaRecorder bindings** plus a completed `Dom_html.mediaElement` by [@hhugo](https://github.com/hhugo) ([#2401](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2401))
- A refreshed stdlib 5.6 snapshot for OCaml trunk changes in `tests-full` was merged by [Jérôme Vouillon](https://github.com/vouillon) ([#2428](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2428))
latest_week.discussions_summary: Review discussion on the Introcaml introspection prototype weighed performance, code-size, and DevTools integration tradeoffs.
latest_week.notable_discussions:
- On the Introcaml JavaScript-introspection prototype, [Frédéric Bour](https://github.com/let-def) raised three review concerns before considering it for merge: performance impact on VM optimizations, potential generated-code bloat from more verbose object allocation, and whether to integrate with `devtoolsFormatters` for pretty-printed objects in browser DevTools ([#2430](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2430))
- [@hhugo](https://github.com/hhugo) followed up with a detailed writeup of two upstream Introcaml limitations found while testing the DevTools formatter — float blocks printing incompletely due to a word-size assumption, and constant all-float records lacking a block descriptor — including suggested fixes for the Introcaml side ([#2430](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2430))
- First-time contributor [habakan](https://github.com/habakan) filed a detailed root-cause report tracing a Safari 17 `Int64.of_string` failure back to a JavaScriptCore parsing quirk with `static` field line breaks, then submitted the fix and, after [@hhugo](https://github.com/hhugo)'s review request, added a code comment explaining the non-obvious `non_breaking_space` choice ([#2420](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2420), [#2421](https://github.com/ocsigen/js_of_ocaml/issues/2421))

latest_week.brief_summary: Runtime-5-only cleanup, DWARF-5 line/location table work, void-record support, and continued LTO/Merlin-diagnostics prototyping dominated the week.
latest_week.new_features_summary: DWARF-5 output selection, `@ read`-mode Bigarray accessors, all-void records, and removal of legacy runtime-4 shims landed.
latest_week.new_features:
- `Bigarray` `Genarray`/`Array0`/`Array1`/`Array2` `get`, `unsafe_get`, and `blit` now require only `@ read` access instead of `@ shared`, letting read-only callers avoid taking a full shared lock on the array ([#5768](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/5768))
- DWARF-5 debug output is now selectable and functional via a `-gdwarf-version` flag by [Mark Shinwell](https://github.com/mshinwell) ([#6923](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6923)), with follow-up work registering the source file as DWARF-5 line-table file 0 on macOS ([#7021](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7021)) and using base-address/offset pairs in DWARF-5 location and range lists ([#6926](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6926))
- All-`void` records (records whose fields are entirely `void`-layout) are now permitted by [Will Sturgeon](https://github.com/wrsturgeon) ([#7070](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7070))
- Non-scanned unboxed layouts (`bits8`/`16`/`32`/`64`, `float32`, `float64`, `untagged_immediate`, `vec128`/`256`/`512`, `void`, `word`) now cross externality inherently rather than requiring a syntactic `mod external_` annotation, by [Ryan Tjoa](https://github.com/rtjoa) ([#6973](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6973))
- Legacy OCaml-runtime-4 support markers were removed by [Nick Barnes](https://github.com/NickBarnes) ([#6707](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6707)): `Config.runtime5` and the deprecated `Gc.eventlog_pause`/`Gc.eventlog_resume` functions are gone, and `Unix.file_descr`'s kind annotation was simplified from `immediate mod contended portable` to plain `immediate`
- `const` qualifiers were added to `argv` in the `caml_startup` C entry points by [Nick Barnes](https://github.com/NickBarnes) ([#4882](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/4882))
- Fixed an allocation-pointer bug that could trigger on stack overflow ([#7020](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7020)) and corrected C stack alignment on stack overflow ([#7088](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7088)), both by [Nick Barnes](https://github.com/NickBarnes)
- Fixed `[@unboxable]` crashing on local parameters when the enclosing function is not local-returning, by [Nathanaëlle Courant](https://github.com/Ekdohibs) ([#6592](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6592))
- CFG dead-code elimination no longer deletes atomic loads whose result is discarded, preserving their side effects, by [Xavier Clerc](https://github.com/xclerc) ([#7101](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7101))
- Cmm peephole optimisations now consistently use the preferred input form ([#7111](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7111)) by [Vincent Laviron](https://github.com/lthls), fixing the `-Oclassic` Cmm crash reported in [#7102](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7102)
- Switches sharing the same destination with many arguments are now merged, reducing generated code size, by [Basile Clément](https://github.com/bclement-ocp) ([#6784](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6784))
- Improved codegen for `Iarray.split` and `Iarray.split_local` by [Nailen Matschke](https://github.com/nmatschke) ([#7116](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7116))
- N-way join performance improvements landed by [Basile Clément](https://github.com/bclement-ocp) ([#6681](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6681)), closing the tracking issue [#6586](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6586)
- Error message wording changed from "mode" to "kind" in the with-on-right-kind diagnostic for clarity, by [Matthew Dempsky](https://github.com/mdempsky) ([#7124](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7124))
- Merlin's `Pmod_hole` construct was upstreamed into the compiler by [David Allsopp](https://github.com/dra27-js) ([#6960](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6960))

latest_week.activity:
- Link-time-optimization (LTO) prototyping continued heavily this week, with [Simon Spies](https://github.com/spiessimon) opening a consolidated LTO-prototype PR ([#7156](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7156)) plus supporting pieces on batched rebuilds ([#7128](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7128)), keeping data symbols global ([#7130](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7130)), disabling `-Oclassic` during LTO ([#7131](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7131)), and backports of slot-offset and code-metadata changes ([#7134](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7134), [#7140](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7140)), while [Miriam Vellacott](https://github.com/mirivella) opened PRs to make the Reaper assume a closed world under LTO ([#7144](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7144)), compute calling-convention changes at solve time ([#7142](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7142)), and store less data in `.cmr`/`.ltosol`/`.reaped.cmx` files ([#7177](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7177))
- Mode-polymorphism and typed-diagnostics work opened several new PRs from [Gavin Gray](https://github.com/gavinleroy), including modality printing relative to explicit defaults ([#7170](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7170)), importing moregen return-mode changes into Merlin ([#7169](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7169)), and allowing skipping of intermediate return modes in moregen ([#7168](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7168)), alongside [ainageorges](https://github.com/ainageorges) opening functor mode variables in `.cmi` files ([#7157](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7157)) and printing/hiding a mode-polymorphic curry mode ([#7098](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7098))
- CFG backend optimization work continued from [Xavier Clerc](https://github.com/xclerc), opening store-to-load forwarding for CFG CSE ([#7123](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7123)) and merging of adjacent `Ioffset_loc` instructions on amd64 ([#7132](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7132)), following earlier merges this week adding CSE across join points ([#6832](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6832)) and dead-store elimination ([#7127](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7127)) to the CFG backend
- Jkind/sort-variable refactoring opened by [Jakub Bachurski](https://github.com/jbachurski), overhauling sort-variable levels ([#7179](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7179)) and adding `moregen_occur` for sort variables ([#7178](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7178)), following the merge of "Untangle equating sorts" ([#6886](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6886))
- [Joe Kerrigan](https://github.com/joe-kerrigan) opened support for layout-polymorphic records and variants ([#7152](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7152)), and [Zack Eisbach](https://github.com/zackbach) opened support for mixed tuples, extending tuple-related data definitions with `Jkind.Sort.t`s to de-duplicate frontend handling of unboxed and boxed tuples ([#7135](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7135))
- Nick Barnes continued garbage-collector and runtime infrastructure work, opening PRs to measure the speed of marking, sweeping, and compaction ([#7161](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7161)), remove the old compaction algorithm ([#7160](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7160)), fix the GC idle phase so `Gc.major_slice()` always advances the GC ([#7158](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7158)), and establish a single source of truth for struct offsets in asm stubs ([#7122](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7122))
- [Robin Ricard](https://github.com/rricard) merged a series of PRs vendoring external tooling directly into the repository as subtrees, including js_of_ocaml (import history, subtree reset, apply patching, compile in the repo: [#6968](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6968), [#7071](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7071), [#7073](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7073), [#7074](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7074)), sedlex ([#7060](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7060), [#7061](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7061), [#7062](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7062)), ppxlib and ppxlib_jane ([#7014](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7014), [#7053](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7053), [#7054](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7054), [#7017](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7017), [#7018](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7018)), and ocaml-compiler-libs ([#7011](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7011), [#7012](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7012))

- Merlin gained a `module-type-impls` query from [Gavin Gray](https://github.com/gavinleroy) to support the Interface Strengthener ([#6811](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6811)), and kind-template module coercions were opened by [Jakub Bachurski](https://github.com/jbachurski) to support layout-polymorphic module item subsumption ([#6792](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6792))
latest_week.discussions_summary: Review threads on the Merlin `module-type-impls` query and kind-template coercions surfaced design questions about API shape and diff scope.
latest_week.notable_discussions:
- On the `module-type-impls` Merlin query ([#6811](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6811)), [Liam Stevenson](https://github.com/liam923) questioned surprising signature-substitution behavior and pushed for a variable-argument loop instead of repeated manual `$MERLIN single module-type-impls` invocations in tests, while also flagging what looked like an AI-generated prompt that had leaked into a commit message
- Reviewers on kind-template module coercions ([#6792](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/6792)) from [Zesen Qian](https://github.com/riaqn) discussed whether unrelated reformatting diffs should be avoided to keep `git blame` usable, and whether `kindtemplate_coercion`'s invariant that `tc_args`/`tc_params` are never the identity permutation should be encoded in the type
- [Rudi Grinberg](https://github.com/rgrinberg) reported that `Persistent_env` checks an imported interface's CRC vector twice on a checked cold lookup, with a proposed patch caching a per-import "already checked" flag to avoid the redundant traversal ([#7114](https://github.com/oxcaml/oxcaml/issues/7114))

latest_week.new_features_summary: Added `Process.environment`/`getenv_opt`, a new `Eio_unix.File` module, and Windows rename plus NT path/stat fixes.
latest_week.new_features:
- Added `Eio.Process.environment` and `Eio.Process.getenv_opt` to the process manager for reading environment variables, with `Env.get_opt` changed to return `None` rather than raising `Invalid_argument` for invalid names, by [Patrick Ferris](https://github.com/patricoferris) with review from [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) and [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([#923](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/923))

- Windows backend gained `rename` support, handling Win32's differing overwrite semantics for files versus directories (FAT volumes cannot replace a directory), by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([#934](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/934))
- Windows NT path handling and `stat`/symlink fixes: corrected an uninitialized-handle check in the `openat`/`unlinkat` stubs that misreported failures, fixed `nofollow` dropping directory/non-directory constraints so `stat` kinds worked again, fixed ELOOP symlink recovery resolving against the process directory instead of the sandbox root, fixed unmapped `Unix` errors escaping `open_in`, stopped `stat` from creating a missing file, and made `stat ~follow:false` actually avoid following the link, resolving [#931](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/931), by [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) ([#932](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/932))
- Fixed a gcc `calloc-transposed-args` warning in `fork_action.c` by [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) ([#933](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/933))
latest_week.activity_summary: A large Windows process-spawning PR opened for review while environment, file-import, rename, and NT-path PRs merged; pipe support remains a work in progress.
latest_week.activity:
- [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) opened **Windows process spawning support** ([#936](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/936)), layered on the still-open pipes fix ([#929](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/929)); [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) gave detailed review feedback on the child-wait/cancellation logic, suggesting a simplified `Fiber.fork_daemon` pattern modeled on `eio_posix`'s existing approach
- **Environment variable access**, a new **`Eio_unix.File` module**, **Windows rename**, a **gcc warning fix**, and **Windows NT path/stat fixes** all merged this week ([#923](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/923), [#937](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/937), [#934](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/934), [#933](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/933), [#932](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/932))

- Issue [#935](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/935), an intermittent `eio_linux` spawn failure with `Unix.EUNKNOWNERR 26` (`ETXTBSY`), was closed after [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) and [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) traced it to an upstream `io_uring` kernel bug, reproduced it directly against `liburing`, and got confirmation from the maintainer that a fix is planned for kernel 7.4
- Issue [#931](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/931), Windows paths being passed unqualified to `NtCreateFile`, was closed via the fixes in [#932](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/932), verified against the `ocaml-forester` test suite in collaboration with [Kento Okura](https://github.com/kentookura)
- Issue [#925](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/925), a request for hard-link support (`Eio.Path.link`) using `linkat` to avoid TOCTOU races when extracting untrusted OCI tar archives, remains open, with [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) noting it is queued behind the Windows symlink work
latest_week.discussions_summary: Debugging of an intermittent eio_linux spawn failure was traced to a confirmed upstream io_uring kernel bug.
latest_week.notable_discussions:
- Investigation into [#935](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/935) combined `bpftrace` kernel tracing and a minimal C reproduction against `liburing` to show that a file descriptor closed before `execve` was nonetheless still considered open by the kernel on ZFS (but not ext4); [Jens Axboe](https://x.com/axboe) confirmed it as a known `io_uring` kernel bug with a fix planned for 7.4, so no change was needed in eio itself
- Design discussion on [#923](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/923) between [Patrick Ferris](https://github.com/patricoferris) and [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) over whether environment access should live on `Eio.Process.mgr` or a separate `Vars` capability, settled by benchmarking `get_all`/`get_opt` versus a direct accessor and by the observation that anyone spawning processes already has environment access
- Review of [#936](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/936) surfaced a discussion on correct cancellation semantics for waiting on a Windows child process, with [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) proposing a `Fiber.fork_daemon`-based pattern that signals the process on switch cancellation while still awaiting its exit

latest_week.emerging_trends:
- Continued concentration of effort on **Windows backend completeness** — process spawning ([#936](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/936)), anonymous pipes ([#929](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/929)), rename ([#934](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/934)), and NT path/stat handling ([#932](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/932), [#931](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/931)) — driven by regression testing against the real-world `ocaml-forester` project with [Kento Okura](https://github.com/kentookura)
- Recurring attention to **capability-safety** in filesystem APIs, seen both in the Windows symlink/stat fixes in [#932](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/932) and in the hard-link request in [#925](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/925), which asks for `linkat`-based semantics to avoid TOCTOU races when extracting untrusted archives
latest_week.contributors_summary: Anil Madhavapeddy, Thomas Leonard, Patrick Ferris, Thomas Gazagnaire, and Kento Okura contributed code, reviews, and issue reports this week.
latest_week.contributors:
- [Anil Madhavapeddy](https://github.com/avsm) opened the Windows process-spawning PR ([#936](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/936)) and merged the Windows rename ([#934](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/934)) and NT path/stat fixes ([#932](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/932)), kept the anonymous-pipes fix ([#929](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/929)) in progress, investigated the upstream `io_uring` bug behind [#935](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/935) including bisecting and reproducing it in C, reviewed [#923](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/923), and discussed the hard-link request in [#925](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/925)
- [Thomas Leonard](https://github.com/talex5) authored and merged the `Eio_unix.File` module ([#937](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/937)) and the gcc warning fix ([#933](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/933)), opened and helped diagnose the `io_uring` spawn bug ([#935](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/935)), and provided detailed review feedback on [#936](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/936), [#923](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/923), and [#932](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/932)
- [Patrick Ferris](https://github.com/patricoferris) implemented the `Eio.Process` environment-variable functions, including benchmarking different API shapes for performance ([#923](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/pull/923))
- [Thomas Gazagnaire](https://github.com/samoht) reported the hard-link capability gap encountered while implementing OCI image extraction ([#925](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/925))
- [Kento Okura](https://github.com/kentookura) reported the Windows `NtCreateFile` path-qualification bug and helped verify the fix by exercising it against the `ocaml-forester` test suite ([#931](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/931))

oldest_week.new_features_summary: Made fork_action.h public header for external libraries and improved Windows symlink test compatibility
oldest_week.new_features:
- **Public header exposure** for `fork_action.h` enabling external libraries to provide new fork actions by [Patrick Ferris](https://github.com/patricoferris) ([#769](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/769))
- **Windows symlink test compatibility** check using `Unix.has_symlink()` to skip symlink tests on systems without support by [Onah_Anthony](https://github.com/create2000) ([#771](https://github.com/ocaml-multicore/eio/issues/771))
oldest_week.activity_summary: New PRs opened for Process.pipe type relaxation and Windows test improvements, ongoing Windows compatibility work
